Support our work to end the Electoral College forever with $25 or whatever you can right now >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=072226_3&amount=25]

➜ Every day, new leaders join our movement, which means we can abolish the Electoral College and give us a true democracy

Too much is at stake for us to give up now.

Mainers have spoken: I am incredibly proud to be their choice for Democratic nominee in our U.S. Senate race.
My name is Troy Jackson. Growing up in Allagash, I didn’t think I’d ever be anything other than a fifth-generation logger. And for a long time, that was more than enough.
But then I got a political education. Not in some Ivy League university — when I was working in the North Woods, grinding out 80-hour workweeks under the thumb of a billionaire. In those woods I discovered the truth: working class people in this country aren’t struggling to get by because we’re not trying hard enough, or not smart enough, or not anything enough. We’re getting crushed by a rigged system, and we have been for way too long.
I got into politics after a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages.
I stayed because once I was there, it was clear that nobody in power understood the actual hardships I’d been living my whole life. Working class people deserve to have someone who lives these struggles in rooms where decisions are being made.
Since then I’ve fought to lower the cost of prescription drugs, pass universal school meals, expand rural healthcare, protect abortion rights, and deliver tax relief. And we’ve won a lot of those fights. But there’s always been someone with more power stepping in to water down or block our progress, or dictate just how far we could go. That’s what happens when our politicians can be bought by corporations and billionaires.
So now it’s time to take this fight to Washington.
Susan Collins is the most vulnerable GOP senator — and for good reason. Her voting record is a disaster. Mainers just can’t trust her to look out for our best interests.
I’m ready to win this, but I’m gonna need you by my side. Will you split a donation of any amount between my campaign and Equal Opportunity Now so we can get ready to win big in November and keep this movement going? A new poll just landed, and here's the headline: I am **one point behind Deb Haaland.** 45% to 46%. That's a statistical dead heat — well within the margin of error.
Michelle Lujan Grisham won this state by double digits. Now, in a race against a former Biden Cabinet secretary with the full weight of the Democratic machine behind her, we are tied.But here's the number that should really get your attention.
When voters in that same poll were simply told the truth about who I am — a New Mexican for 40 years, a small business owner who built a company from scratch, and the longest-serving Mayor in Rio Rancho's history — the race flips. **I lead Deb Haaland 49% to 43%.**
Read that again. A six-point swing, just from voters hearing my actual record instead of whatever Haaland and her allies want them to believe.
That's the whole campaign in one number. This race isn't close because New Mexicans want more of the same — it's close because we haven't finished telling my story yet. Every doubt she wants to plant, and every DC-funded ad she's about to run against me, has one job: to keep voters from hearing what that poll just proved works.
I need the resources to make sure they hear it — on TV, on the radio, in their mailbox, everywhere.
Can you chip in $25, $50, or $100 right now to help me close that gap for good?

| **WHO REALLY KILLED FIRST BRANDS Pt 5: Two Executives Have Confessed ** [](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=oqqk50t2l01m7dsdre9&linkid=1&link=8f099b3cab14400caa73efe76186e0a7) [Part 1](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=oqqk50t2l01m7dsdre9&linkid=2&link=6be0d2b34f8d46c993bdcab2bb175cce) examined the destruction of First Brands, the indictment of its founder Patrick James. [Part 2](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=oqqk50t2l01m7dsdre9&linkid=3&link=e552261afa104614b0e17725c6ca6d27) examined the federal prosecution and the cooperators on whom the government's case rests. [Part 3 ](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=oqqk50t2l01m7dsdre9&linkid=4&link=8fafdd5df60b40669dbf196c13054767)examined Apollo Global Management, a trillion-dollar Wall Street firm with annual revenue, in recent years, of between $26 billion and $33 billion [Part 4](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=oqqk50t2l01m7dsdre9&linkid=5&link=9bca368c2f8b4390a41bea0def5dd280) examined Apollo's bet against First Brands, its competing auto-parts holdings, and the conflict of its former chairman now prosecuting the case.
### **_This is Part 5_**
First Brands made auto parts. FRAM oil filters. Raybestos brakes. Autolite spark plugs. Trico wiper blades. It owned two dozen American brands and employed six thousand Americans and nineteen thousand more around the world. Last fall, First Brands collapsed seemingly overnight. It had $12 million in cash. It owed almost $11 billion. A cash-to-debt ratio of this size is among the largest corporate gaps. That would be like a family with $1,200 in the bank, owing $1.1 million. Patrick James founded First Brands in 2013. Twelve years later, in September 2025, First Brands filed for bankruptcy. Once a company enters bankruptcy, its founder no longer runs it. Control passes to the lawyers and financial advisers. They are paid by the hour. Before it was over, they would bill close to a quarter of a billion dollars. What happened to First Brands? That was the question a bankruptcy court appointed an investigator to answer.
## **_The Invoices That Never Were_**
Here is the fraud the bankruptcy records appear to prove. It was simple. It had everything to do with borrowing money. First Brands borrowed against invoices that didn't exist. No customer placed an order. No parts were shipped. Someone in the company simply typed up a phony invoice -- a customer's name, an amount, an invoice number -- for a sale that never happened, and sold that fraudulent piece of paper to a factor for money. The examiner found $1.4 billion in such invoices: bills the company's records showed no sign of, because the sales were not real. To understand how that worked, start with what factoring is. Factoring is selling money you're owed today for slightly less than it's worth. For instance, say First Brands ships $1 million in brake parts to Walmart. Walmart will pay in 90 days. First Brands needs cash now. So it sells the unpaid bill to a third company, called a factor. The factor pays First Brands $970,000 today, then waits and collects the full $1 million from Walmart later. That $30,000 is the factor's fee for the three-month wait -- about 3 percent per quarter, which works out to roughly 12 percent per year. First Brands' real factoring ran far steeper than that: the examiner found rates of 20 to 30 percent. On money out for only a few months, that is a high return, which is part of why so many lenders kept loaning money against invoices to First Brands. First Brands was, in part, a company that borrowed too much, too fast, at too high a price. It grew by buying other companies by borrowing money, piling up interest, and repayment obligations**.** The examiner found the high rates were not just the cost of fast growth. They reflected, in his words, the company's "desperate liquidity needs" -- a business so starved for cash that it would pay almost any price to keep money coming in. The expensive borrowing was both a cause of the collapse and a symptom of a company that had to keep borrowing to hide the fraud.
## **_The Same Bill, Sold Twice_**
Sometimes First Brands sold the same bill to two different factors. In its case, the factors weren't collecting from Walmart. First Brands had kept itself in the middle. Walmart paid First Brands. First Brands paid the factors. So no factor was watching for a customer payment that never came. They were watching for First Brands to pay them. First Brands always did, but with money from the next round of fraud. New factoring paid off old factoring. As long as First Brands could keep fabricating and selling fresh invoices, it could keep paying everyone it owed. The examiner found that the money repaying the factors often came not from real customer collections but from new financing. For five years, every payment arrived on time. A system like that only runs while new cash flows in faster than old bills come due. When it stopped -- when the factoring stopped because of the bankruptcy in September 2025 -- there was nothing left to pay anyone. The $11 billion in obligations met $12 million in cash. The collapse arrived at once. First Brands also inflated invoices -- taking a genuine invoice and fraudulently padding the amount. A $5,000 sale was sold to a factor as $9,000, pulling out cash on money that no customer was obligated to pay. Another method was off-balance-sheet financing -- borrowing money in a way that doesn't appear on the balance sheet as a loan. A company's financial statements list what it owns and what it owes. Lenders read those statements before they lend. If a company owes too much, no one wants to lend it more. First Brands set up separate companies -- shell companies it controlled but kept off its books. Carnaby, Broad Street, and others, set up to hold inventory and take loans without the debt appearing on First Brands' books. These were built with real credit agreements, real lenders, and opinion letters from a major law firm. The shells "owned" piles of inventory: brake pads, filters, parts sitting in warehouses. Lenders gave the shells money, secured by that inventory. If a shell couldn't pay, the lender could seize the parts. Two things went wrong, according to the examiner. The inventory pledged to one lender was sometimes pledged to another, or wasn't there at all. The fake invoices, the bills sold twice, the hidden loans -- is the method the investigators found. The question was who did it.
## **The Examiner 's Verdict**
Shortly after the bankruptcy was filed, the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York indicted Patrick James, the company's founder. The charge is that he ran a criminal enterprise of financial fraud out of his company. James faces trial in February 2027. The question the trial must answer is whether James directed the fraud or presided over a company in deep financial trouble, in which others committed fraud. On April 27, 2026, the bankruptcy-court-appointed examiner, Martin De Luca, a partner at Boies Schiller Flexner, answered a narrower question: whether fraud occurred. The answer was yes. Two executives took part in it. Both were charged criminally and have pleaded guilty. Their names are Stephen Graham, First Brands' chief financial officer, and Peter Andrew Brumbergs, its vice president of finance. The one question the bankruptcy investigator could not answer: Was James involved in the fraud? Or was this a scheme, desperate and self-serving, run by two top executives and kept hidden from James? _An Investigator Close to the Prosecutors_ De Luca worked with the U.S. Attorney, he said, to avoid stepping on a criminal case, but ran his own investigation. James's lawyers argue he worked too closely with them. The examiner had regular calls with the U.S. Attorney's office and the FBI and cleared his witnesses with them. He called it deconfliction -- keeping his civil investigation from colliding with the criminal case. James called it a court officer helping a prosecution. An examiner aligned with the government had every reason to deliver the finding the government wanted: that Patrick James personally ran the fraud. De Luca couldn't. He reviewed 14 terabytes of data. His forensic accountants came from Guidepost Solutions. He subpoenaed correspondent banks. Thirteen and a half million documents. Seventy-five witnesses. On the question of whether James directed the fabrication of invoices, the examiner ended **w** ithout proof that James was involved in any fraud.
## **_What He Found, and What He Couldn 't_**
De Luca found First Brands receivables that were "fabricated, repeatedly pledged, or never transferred as represented." He found a company that, in his words, "did not merely become insolvent." He found that it "was used as a financial engine for generating and extracting liquidity through structures that concealed the enterprise's true perimeter and depleted value otherwise available to creditors." None of this proves James did it. Three serious findings. Only one -- the fabricated invoices -- is plainly a crime on its face. The report shows that Brumbergs committed the crime, not James. The examiner found a company "used as a financial engine" to extract value, but used by whom is the question. Not one of the three places where the wrongdoing was committed was through actions taken by James. The examiner said as much himself. He called his findings colorable -- plausible enough to investigate, not proven. The investigation was paused in mid-February because the court-approved $7 million budget had run out, with substantial work remaining. He asked for 90 more days and more money to confirm what he had found. On June 18, the court denied the budget increase. The investigation stopped. The examiner studied one kind of fraud: the lies First Brands told its lenders and factors. The fraud was real. The company's chief financial officer has pleaded guilty to it. The report named the operators -- and did not name James, the man on trial. Who those operators are -- Graham and Brumbergs -- is the next part of this story. Picture the man the government has to convict. Patrick James built First Brands from nothing into one of the largest auto-parts companies in the world --25 brands, 26,000 employees, factories on five continents. Running a company that size is not a desk job. It is product lines, labor contracts, plant closings, and acquisitions in a dozen countries and as many currencies. No chief executive of a company that large reads the invoices. That is precisely why a company of that size has a chief financial officer and a vice president of finance. Their job is the numbers. His job is everything else. So here is the first question the government cannot dodge: in a company of that scale, who actually committed the fraud? The government's evidence answers it. The answer is not Patrick James. The court's independent examiner reviewed 13.5 million documents and named the men at the controls: Brumbergs at the keyboard, making the entries, modifying the invoices; Brumbergs built a system that rerouted the lenders' emails so that no one else in the company would see them. The man running the scheme built a wall to keep James and other employees from finding out. The chief financial officer and the vice president of finance have pleaded guilty. They have admitted, under oath, that they made false statements, misrepresented the company's condition, and processed fraudulent invoices. The men whose literal job was the company's books have confessed to corrupting them. And Patrick James? A bankruptcy judge looked at the company's best evidence against him in November and said it from the bench: "There's nothing showing that James, himself, was manipulating invoices." Five months later, the examiner -- an investigator working hand in glove with the prosecutors, with every incentive to deliver the man at the top -- could not get there either. He did not find James's hand in the fraud. If the judge could not see it, and the prosecutor-friendly expert examiner could not prove it after 13.5 million documents, what, exactly, is left? What is left is the word of two confessed criminals who have not yet been sentenced. That is the case. To convict James of directing this fraud, the government must put on the stand the very men who built it -- men who pleaded guilty to running the scheme, whose punishment has been postponed until after they testify, and who understand, as any person in the cooperator's chair would understand, that the prosecutors holding the keys to their sentence are the prosecutors who want a conviction. The jury will be told to weigh such testimony with caution. It should. These are not bystanders who happened to see something. They are the architects of the fraud, testifying for their freedom, against the one man whose conviction buys it for them.
## **The Note, and the Money**
The government will wave a single note -- "Talked with PJ" -- written not by James but by the CFO, Graham, describing a conversation, listing accounting adjustments. The jury will be asked to read Graham's note as proof that James ordered a crime. But a CEO who wants restructuring costs presented one way rather than another is doing what CEOs do. The note does not say "fabricate an invoice." It does not say "lie to a lender." To make it mean that, the government needs Graham, the man who wrote it -- a man pleading for his sentence -- to stand up and tell the jury it meant that. The note is not proof. It is an invitation to trust a cooperator. The money. Yes, money flowed to Patrick James. He owned the company. Owners take distributions. They pay themselves dividends. With a company structured as his was, they must pull cash simply to pay the taxes the company runs up in their name. The government calls it "siphoning." But it has not shown the company was insolvent on the day of any transfer, which is what would turn a lawful distribution into a crime. It has not subtracted the hundreds of millions James put back in. It counted the money going out and stopped counting. A number by itself is not theft. So this is the question the jury will be asked. It is not the question the headlines asked, not the question the bankruptcy made easy, but the actual question the law puts to 12 citizens: Did the government prove, beyond a reasonable doubt, that Patrick James -- not his finance chiefs, but James himself -- knew the cash was the product of fraud and chose to direct it? Or did it prove only what everyone already concedes: that a fraud occurred, that two confessed criminals ran it, that a company drowning in debt finally went under, and that the owner, like every owner, took money out of the business he built? If the honest answer to the first question is "we cannot be sure" -- if the case for James's guilt rests on a note he did not write and the testimony of two men buying their freedom -- then there is only one verdict the law allows. He is presumed innocent. The government must erase all reasonable doubt. On the question that matters -- not whether First Brands was a fraud, but whether Patrick James directed it -- the doubt is not at the edges of this case. It is the center of it. By Frank Parlato - [https://artvoice.com/who-really-killed-first-brands-pt-5-two-execs-confessed](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=oqqk50t2l01m7dsdre9&linkid=6&link=021707590e8a4084b7d9f02d5e464889)

Or did it prove only what everyone already concedes: that a fraud occurred, that two confessed criminals ran it, that a company drowning in debt finally went under, and that the owner, like every owner, took money out of the business he built? If the honest answer to the first question is "we cannot be sure" -- if the case for James's guilt rests on a note he did not write and the testimony of two men buying their freedom -- then there is only one verdict the law allows. He is presumed innocent. The government must erase all reasonable doubt. On the question that matters -- not whether First Brands was a fraud, but whether Patrick James directed it -- the doubt is not at the edges of this case. It is the center of it. By Frank Parlato - | ] ] ] ] Sent using [ [DirectIQ ] ](=)

For 250 years, America has been the greatest nation on Earth - not because government made us great, but because freedom did.
We became a magnet for the most talented, hardworking people in the world. We rewarded innovation. We celebrated success. We believed that if you worked hard and played by the rules, you could build a better life for yourself and your family.
That's the America I grew up believing in.
Unfortunately, there are people today who want to take us in a different direction.
The modern Left is increasingly embracing the failed ideas of socialism, government dependency, and resentment toward those who succeed. They don't want to expand opportunity - they want to redistribute it.

**I’m excited to let you know about our online course, “Marxism, Socialism, and Communism,”[now available on DVD](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuK3DAQRb9G3tnoZcu98CLE41VmhoSQXhpZqnYX6IUldfL5wWDyAdndqgvnQNX9fX3X6DDsH9rDhDmvNto11sPHXNCneBQdSgwOA5hYV0750FLVcr5qU_AFq9SNnXrOxsfYwMTUKNWgVD80z4k97MYeQz8ysQGVTGzDbaCqp5uS26Z4g9PJo4oLSuWNic5a-uA3RnspR5CSEUlrsrpAhyGjhWxiTCk6LGhyF4-9cdOzlJSJ-EL4QviSwdQDbPdE57LVDjqwlfDl30z44vXxB7NvczSo3ZlM9L6GM9mXJWLJhoiZsqG_fVAu-bdfn_Pn_Pb2lfChFr_mWA8DRMzpiDmBKRj2q_JgsXoiZvAa3bU02ieNeyBivtzr6bnKGAqEQsT8XbX3nz_a6ya8OSabfqNzmAdFJN1PYmeib8r_fuo18b8BAAD__-FGpaw)!**

Today, Marxism goes by different names to make itself seem less dangerous. I'm sure you've heard of "critical race theory," "gender theory," or even "decolonization."

I know these disguises do not fool you.

"Marxism, Socialism, and Communism" is one of our most important courses **because the source of these dangerous ideologies is still Karl Marx.**

It’s the same Marxism that works to destroy your property and your country.

It’s the same Marxism that seeks to abolish your family and your God.

And it’s the same Marxism that leads to famines, show trials, gulags, and other atrocities.

The truth is, there’s nothing fundamentally _new_ about this "new" Marxism, except for one crucial fact...

**... it's more popular with our youth than ever before.**

By way of example, the mayor of our largest city vowed to replace “rugged individualism” with the “warmth of collectivism.” Clearly, this issue isn’t going away.

That's why I invite you to gain a deeper understanding of the history of Marxism as well as the threat it poses to our liberty.

[**You can do that by requesting your copy of “Marxism, Socialism, and Communism” today.**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuK3DAQRb9G3tnoZcu98CLE41VmhoSQXhpZqnYX6IUldfL5wWDyAdndqgvnQNX9fX3X6DDsH9rDhDmvNto11sPHXNCneBQdSgwOA5hYV0750FLVcr5qU_AFq9SNnXrOxsfYwMTUKNWgVD80z4k97MYeQz8ysQGVTGzDbaCqp5uS26Z4g9PJo4oLSuWNic5a-uA3RnspR5CSEUlrsrpAhyGjhWxiTCk6LGhyF4-9cdOzlJSJ-EL4QviSwdQDbPdE57LVDjqwlfDl30z44vXxB7NvczSo3ZlM9L6GM9mXJWLJhoiZsqG_fVAu-bdfn_Pn_Pb2lfChFr_mWA8DRMzpiDmBKRj2q_JgsXoiZvAa3bU02ieNeyBivtzr6bnKGAqEQsT8XbX3nz_a6ya8OSabfqNzmAdFJN1PYmeib8r_fuo18b8BAAD__-FGpaw)

**[https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/marxism-socialism-communism-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuK3DAQRb9G3tnoZcu98CLE41VmhoSQXhpZqnYX6IUldfL5wWDyAdndqgvnQNX9fX3X6DDsH9rDhDmvNto11sPHXNCneBQdSgwOA5hYV0750FLVcr5qU_AFq9SNnXrOxsfYwMTUKNWgVD80z4k97MYeQz8ysQGVTGzDbaCqp5uS26Z4g9PJo4oLSuWNic5a-uA3RnspR5CSEUlrsrpAhyGjhWxiTCk6LGhyF4-9cdOzlJSJ-EL4QviSwdQDbPdE57LVDjqwlfDl30z44vXxB7NvczSo3ZlM9L6GM9mXJWLJhoiZsqG_fVAu-bdfn_Pn_Pb2lfChFr_mWA8DRMzpiDmBKRj2q_JgsXoiZvAa3bU02ieNeyBivtzr6bnKGAqEQsT8XbX3nz_a6ya8OSabfqNzmAdFJN1PYmeib8r_fuo18b8BAAD__-FGpaw)**

subject: The numbers should alarm every conservative.
body:
Four Republican-held seats are now at risk. Here's why it matters.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)

| | Peter,
**The numbers are in.**
And if you're a conservative who loves Colorado, they should set off alarm bells. Democrats didn't just edge Republicans in this year's primary.
**They dominated.**
Colorado's largest voting bloc, unaffiliated voters, broke for Democrats by a staggering **70 to 30 margin.**
In **CO-08 alone, Democrats cast 31,837 more primary ballots than Republicans** in a district Republicans won by only **2,596 votes** last November.
**Four Republican-held congressional seats are now at risk.**
The Left sees an opportunity to tighten its grip on Colorado.
**We can't let that happen.**

Folks, real talk.
Rep Adam Smith, top Dem on the House Armed Services Committee, co-introduced Section 224 that would functionally merge the US military with Israel's.
He was formally censured for that by the Washington State Democrats by a vote of 600 to 104.
AIPAC, which has been his biggest donor throughout his career by far, check opensecrets.org, thanked him publicly for this.
He flipped under our pressure, but only after he himself killed Rep Ro Khanna's amendment that would have removed Section 224 before the bill even got out of his committee, and he only flipped when he knew that his flip wouldn't do a damn bit of good.
Sure enough, just today, July 22, 2026, the House passed the NDAA that funds our military, and this poison pill that merges the US military with Israel's was buried inside it.
Adam Smith did that.
Meanwhile, Kshama Sawant yells a lot about ending our support for genocide.
She's not wrong.
Problem is, she's not authentic, and she's been lying to you about me.
I have been a heartfelt supporter of the Palestinian people since I was 11 years old. My family has been friends with Rachel Corrie's family for 20 years. My husband, Zahid Chaudhry, is the president of Veterans for Peace, Rachel Corrie chapter. We've marched and held peace vigils for Palestine for literally decades.
And we were out at the front of marches against this genocide starting in October 2023, mere weeks into this, when most folks thought we were crazy. We kept that up all through the summer of 2024. Me, a federal candidate, pregnant, pushing my husband in his wheelchair, our toddler daughter on his lap, up and down Seattle hills, calling for justice and ceasefire at the top of our lungs.
Many of you were there. You know what that took at the time. You know what courage and moral clarity that required. You know the costs we all paid.
I don't remember seeing Kshama with us. Do you?
And if she wants credit for her advocacy now, but wants to undermine, lie about, and attack the person who's lived this most wholeheartedly my entire life, do you trust her?
Because I don't.
And many of my Palestinian friends, organizers, and fellow peace activists don't either. They've told her she's not welcome at their events anymore because she hijacks them for her own politics and doesn't build real relationships.
That's not an ally. That's an opportunist.
Like she seized on my husband's illegal detention by ICE for her own political gain, then tried to claim that I, I who lived this, who fought back against ICE in four federal courts with no lawyers and won, that I don't oppose ICE terror.
Folks, you have an opportunity to vote for the real thing.
The only congressional candidate in the nation who's taken Track AIPAC's PEACE Pledge, seven concrete policy commitments.
My video on that and more of my history of solidarity are at VoteMelissa4Congress.com/videos. You'll see the link in the text.
By every measure, including who's lying about me and trying to kill my genuinely grassroots campaign, I'm the best candidate you have.
Take an honest look. See for yourself.
As I said in my speech at UW during the Liberated Zone in May 2024, "we can free Palestine through political action, but we have to do it together."
Dignity, Safety, Opportunity for all people on all of this earth.
Care. Courage. The Constitution.

* He’s selectively disclosing a cherrypicked set of classified documents that paint a false picture of alleged foreign interference.
* It’s a predictable disinformation playbook to make people doubt the results of future elections — like the ones his party may very well lose this November.

clean_body: What he’s really up to: | | | Last week, Donald Trump got on national TV and gave a prime-time speech from the White House. Usually, when a president does that sort of thing, they have something new and important to say. But honestly, Trump just loves surrounding himself with the trappings of the presidency. He loves hearing the sound of his own voice. And he wanted to invite himself into millions of living rooms to retread desperate lies about the election he lost in 2020 — to lay the groundwork for future attempts to overthrow upcoming elections. Here’s what you need to know (without having to watch him rant and rave): He’s desperate to validate his conspiracy theories about 2020. He’s selectively disclosing a cherrypicked set of classified documents that paint a false picture of alleged foreign interference. * It’s a predictable disinformation playbook to make people doubt the results of future elections — like the ones his party may very well lose this November. subject: I should be homeless, dead or in jail.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MELANIE LUCERO FOR CONGRESS
body:
That's what the statistics said about a girl like me. Here's what happened instead — and why I'm running.
| [ MELANIE LUCERO
FOR CONGRESS · VIRGINIA'S 5TH DISTRICT ](https://us.list-manage.com/1InxImv2Q3W?e=b859d69a85&c2id=840d926fa883d6ae62831c5dde7f0f04)
---
A note from Melanie · 1 of 7
# I wasn't supposed to make it out — let alone run for Congress.
Peter,I grew up with a drug-addicted father — in drug-infested motels and trailer parks, the kind of places you pass on the highway and hope your kids never see the inside of. When I was 15, he was arrested and sentenced to life in prison.And then no one came. The Department of Social Services never checked on me or my brother — not once. We were split up, staying with separate friends for weeks or months at a time, while I finished high school on my own.According to the statistics, I should be homeless, dead, or in jail. But this country affords everyone the chance to make better choices. I made mine.At 18, while my friends were picking dorm rooms, partying or getting in trouble, I signed a contract with the United States Marine Corps. I graduated at the top of my class and served as an Intelligence Analyst — work where you don't get points for trying. You get results, or people get hurt, or even worse, they don't go home to their families.After the Corps, I served in the Intelligence Community supporting counter-terrorism operations domestically and worldwide. Then I came to Virginia, married my husband Michael, and built a real estate business at Lake Anna helping families find the place they call home.So why am I running? Because the 5th District is represented by a politician who campaigns like a fighter and governs like a placeholder. John McGuire takes credit for bills other people spent 25 years building. He answers our housing crisis with press releases, not plans. And when a veteran or a senior in this district calls his office for help — the phone just rings.I know what it's like when the people who are supposed to show up for you never do. I promised myself I'd never be one of them. That's why my office will treat your call like a mission — because to your family, it is one.Between now and **August 4** , I'll send you a handful of short notes — two minutes each — on exactly where I stand. No spin, no 27 fundraising links. Read them, then decide if I've earned your vote. | [Read My Full Story](https://us.list-manage.com/T1vNYGtOUCi?e=b859d69a85&c2id=840d926fa883d6ae62831c5dde7f0f04)
---
Takes two minutes — the whole story, start to finish.
* * *
Semper Fi,
Melanie Lucero
Marine Veteran · Republican for Congress, VA-05

name: Phil Izon
subject: Polling locations, ballots, senate and house districts with address search
body:
907Honest.com for Alaska News, Politics, History, and more. | | | [](https://q8w2.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a61b87114a24b4e78e5c731&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.907honest.com%2F%3Fss_source%3Dsscampaigns%26ss_campaign_id%3D6a61b642aa16280472f7a90d%26ss_email_id%3D6a61b87114a24b4e78e5c731%26ss_campaign_name%3DPolling%2Blocations%252C%2Bballots%252C%2Bsenate%2Band%2Bhouse%2Bdistricts%2Bwith%2Baddress%2Bsearch%26ss_campaign_sent_date%3D2026-07-23T06%253A45%253A30Z&w=69a52c74bc7495054af302fd&c=b_6a61b642aa16280472f7a90d&l=en-US&s=t-2-idbVenTQK4-QE4PPMZywkSs%3D)
---
| **When a citizen has to hop across three different non-communicating web portals just to answer three basic questions,** **Where do I vote?** **What district am I in?** **What will my ballot look like?** **a significant portion of voters simply give up. By consolidating address searching, district mapping, polling locations, and ballot previews into a single interactive layer, 907Honest.com removes massive friction from civic participation.** **Here are key lessons from comparing state-run digital infrastructure with agile, independent builder projects:** **1\. Siloed Systems vs. User-Centric Design Government:** **State agency websites are typically built around administrative structure, not user journeys.** **The Division of Elections maintains a lookup table, the Redistricting Board hosts the boundary maps, and a third department handles voter registration. Each team manages its own contract, software stack, and database.** **Private/Civic Tech: Starts with one core question ("How do I get a voter everything they need in two clicks?") and unifies the underlying data sources behind a single search query.** **2\. Procurement Bloat vs. Lean Stack Government:** **Updating a public-facing portal often requires RFP (Request for Proposal) processes, security reviews, inter-departmental approvals, and multi-year vendor contracts. By the time a feature is deployed, the tech stack is already outdated.** **Civic Builders: A single developer can tap open GIS data layers, geocoding APIs, and static document links to build a modern vector-mapped web app over a weekend for pennies.** **3\. "Functional Compliance" vs. "Actual Usability" Government compliance:** **The state's legal requirement is simply to make the information publicly available. A searchable PDF table or static JPEG map technically fulfills the law.** **User expectation: Modern web users expect spatial awareness, typing an address, seeing a pin on a map, and getting contextually relevant links instantly.** **Compliance does not equal good UX. The Big Takeaway: Information accessibility is a form of voter access.** **When government systems make information hard to navigate, it creates artificial barriers.** **Independent builders using open data are often the most effective force for modernizing civic infrastructure.**
---

clean_body: 907Honest.com for Alaska News, Politics, History, and more. | | | | When a citizen has to hop across three different non-communicating web portals just to answer three basic questions, Where do I vote? What district am I in? What will my ballot look like? a significant portion of voters simply give up. By consolidating address searching, district mapping, polling locations, and ballot previews into a single interactive layer, 907Honest.com removes massive friction from civic participation. Here are key lessons from comparing state-run digital infrastructure with agile, independent builder projects: 1\. Siloed Systems vs. User-Centric Design Government: State agency websites are typically built around administrative structure, not user journeys. The Division of Elections maintains a lookup table, the Redistricting Board hosts the boundary maps, and a third department handles voter registration. Each team manages its own contract, software stack, and database. Private/Civic Tech: Starts with one core question ("How do I get a voter everything they need in two clicks?") and unifies the underlying data sources behind a single search query. 2\. Procurement Bloat vs. Lean Stack Government: Updating a public-facing portal often requires RFP (Request for Proposal) processes, security reviews, inter-departmental approvals, and multi-year vendor contracts. By the time a feature is deployed, the tech stack is already outdated. Civic Builders: A single developer can tap open GIS data layers, geocoding APIs, and static document links to build a modern vector-mapped web app over a weekend for pennies. 3\. "Functional Compliance" vs. "Actual Usability" Government compliance: The state's legal requirement is simply to make the information publicly available. A searchable PDF table or static JPEG map technically fulfills the law. User expectation: Modern web users expect spatial awareness, typing an address, seeing a pin on a map, and getting contextually relevant links instantly. Compliance does not equal good UX. The Big Takeaway: Information accessibility is a form of voter access. When government systems make information hard to navigate, it creates artificial barriers. # Through Smoke and Fire
---
| | | _To our Friends and Supporters, _ Most of us reading this and millions of people across the northeastern U.S. have likely had to change summer plans or may be staying inside because of another season of massive fires in the Boundary Waters of Minnesota and northern Ontario and Manitoba. Here on Chequamegon Bay the Madeline Island Ferry had to suspend service at times last week for the first time ever due to zero visibility conditions in heavy smoke.
---
| | |
---
| | | We’ve seen extreme heat and fire conditions around the world this year and severe fire weather is expected to remain for at least several more weeks, placing 2026 in another year of record fire conditions. Entire communities including Canadian First Nations have been burned over and displaced, and hundreds of firefighters from the U.S. and Canada are working to contain these fires. In years past when a neighboring country and one of our strongest allies experienced a natural disaster, members of Congress and our Executive branch would have directed federal agencies to collaborate to provide aid, assistance, and funding. Instead, Rep. Tiffany and his colleagues in the Wisconsin Republican delegation in Congress have written to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin this week asking the EPA to invoke authorities under the U.S. - Canada Air Quality Agreement requesting Canada take undefined steps to reduce fire risk in Canada. This response from Tiffany is essentially like calling your neighbor the day their house is on fire and complaining that it’s ruining your barbeque. It’s noteworthy that these members of Congress are also finally seeing a role for the EPA they find useful - essentially serving as a complaint department for our neighbors. _Whatever happened to standing up in times of crisis to help our neighbors?_ This version of America First actually looks more like America Alone, and most Americans know this is not who we are, and it’s not making us stronger. The fact is, after all these years, Tom Tiffany still doesn't get it. We cannot complain our way to reducing extreme climate disasters, and we cannot log our way out of the growing problem of larger, more intense wildfires. With a changing climate, we are going to see more extreme heat like we've seen this week, more severe wind events, more flash floods, and more extreme wildfires like these in the years ahead. And we need to make the investments today to reduce those risks and respond to those events. But Representative Tiffany has long been one of Washington's most dedicated zealots for disinvesting in the U.S. Forest Service and the other federal agencies that lead our responses to wildfires. And the U.S. Forest Service is right now in the midst of a reorganization that will force thousands more career managers and scientists to leave the agency and reduce our capacity to understand climate change and to respond effectively to wildfires even more.
---
| | |
---
| | | Climate change affects all of us, and it's not going to slow its acceleration without decisive, informed, bold action. Wisconsinites deserve representatives in Congress who understand what's at stake and who will tell the truth about what's happening to our air, water, and land – and who isn't beholden to fossil fuel company lobbyists. I want to go to Washington next year and help do that work for all of us. We'll get through this together if we work together.Please remember our state’s primary election is on August 11th. Please see details on Wisconsin voting in the section below. I hope you’ll make a plan to vote, and I would love to have your support!
---
| | |
---
Fred
---
PS: On Tuesday, I was excited to announce that Congressman Mark Pocan of Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District endorsed my campaign! Mark joins former Wisconsin members of Congress David Obey, Peter Barca, Tom Barrett and Steve Kagan in supporting team Clark. The wind is in our sails and we're less then three weeks until the primary election. Be sure to make a plan to vote on August 11th!

# **_On the Road_**
---
| | | **Tribal Communities Take Center Stage ** Powwows are some of the most important events of the year for tribal communities and an opportunity for members to come together, share traditions, food, music, and dancing, to celebrate achievements, and to recognize losses. The Lac Courte Oreilles Honor the Earth Powwow is all of that, and for hundreds of non-tribal visitors and guests, it's an education in culture and community. Seeing the Grand Entry and all of the men, women, and children dancing in their regalia accompanied by drumming circles is a powerful experience for everyone. Rick St. Germaine invited Fred to speak to the crowd after the Grand Entry where he stressed the importance of having a federal government that follows the Constitution, that respects the dignity of every person on American soil, and that honors the treaties, agreements, and solemn trust obligations we have entered into with native peoples across America. Our words should mean something and nowhere is that responsibility more important than with our commitments with our tribal nations.
---
| |
---
---
---
| | | **Wisconsin Farm Technology Days ** Wisconsin's Farm Technology Days is the biggest agriculture event of the year. Farmers came from all over the state to check out the latest equipment and techniques, and folks from every walk of life showed up just to learn more about where their food comes from. This year in Stratford, it was drones and robotics next to cheese curds and lemonade — a perfect mix for a hot summer day. Our farmers feed our state and our country, and they deserve leaders who understand their challenges and show up for them.If you want to support Wisconsin agriculture, showing up to learn is one of the best places to start. And voting for representatives who will show up for farmers is one of the best ways to make sure their good work continues.
---
| |

# **In the News**
---
| | | **A New Forever War** As the Iran cease fire deal negotiated by the President’s son in law and his billionaire friend Steve Witkopf has predictably fallen apart, the open hostilities in the Iran War have resumed. More American service members have been killed, and control of the Strait of Hormuz is once again being contested, and the prospects for a wider ground war can no longer be ruled out. According to [estimates by the Center for American Progress](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135809298/635434331/2089313517?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjEwMzAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTAzODcyYTctODU4Ni1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=TYTRHUvK-IqjR0-YLSX5kQm7aMU-Edesw94lldODocE=&emci=1fec503c-5484-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=e03872a7-8586-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=28718937), the costs of the Iran war include at least 14 American lives lost and over 400 casualties. Direct costs of military operations could be as much as $100 billion, and Americans have paid more than $68 billion in higher costs for fuel and gasoline since the war began. Longer term economic effects also include increased inflation, especially for any food or manufactured goods, and higher interest rates. These are costs that fall especially heavily on lower income Americans, especially in light of the reduction or elimination of so many federal programs that provide assistance to folks who need it. In this chaotic environment, the Administration has again ignored Congress, making it clear that today’s Congressional leadership is failing at one of their most important constitutional responsibilities. Please keep our American service members and their families in mind and pray for their safety and support. It’s time for new leadership, and the war in Iran reminds of that every day.

But to ensure a smooth election day, we want to provide you with all the information you need to create a plan to vote. The deadline to register to vote online or by mail is July 22nd. The deadline to register at your local clerk’s office is August 7th by 5pm. And, as always, you can register to vote at your polling location on election day. To check if you are registered, you can go to myvote.wi.gov. By entering your name and birthday, you can find your registration status and polling location and request an absentee ballot.August 6th is the deadline for requesting an absentee ballot for most individuals. A completed ballot can be mailed any time before election day, and it is recommended to afford seven days before election day for your ballot to arrive. Your best bet is to drop it off in-person if you are able. In-person absentee (early) voting runs from July 28th through August 9th. You can drop your ballot off or fill one out at your municipal clerk’s office, or at another designated in your town. Check myvote.wi.gov for precise locations for early voting.For the full list of deadlines, check myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Voter-Deadlines. Voting is best done early and with a plan in mind. clean_body: Team Clark battled smokey conditions this week| | | | Through Smoke and Fire | | | To our Friends and Supporters, Most of us reading this and millions of people across the northeastern U.S. have likely had to change summer plans or may be staying inside because of another season of massive fires in the Boundary Waters of Minnesota and northern Ontario and Manitoba. Here on Chequamegon Bay the Madeline Island Ferry had to suspend service at times last week for the first time ever due to zero visibility conditions in heavy smoke. | | | | | | We’ve seen extreme heat and fire conditions around the world this year and severe fire weather is expected to remain for at least several more weeks, placing 2026 in another year of record fire conditions. Entire communities including Canadian First Nations have been burned over and displaced, and hundreds of firefighters from the U.S. and Canada are working to contain these fires. In years past when a neighboring country and one of our strongest allies experienced a natural disaster, members of Congress and our Executive branch would have directed federal agencies to collaborate to provide aid, assistance, and funding. Instead, Rep. Tiffany and his colleagues in the Wisconsin Republican delegation in Congress have written to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin this week asking the EPA to invoke authorities under the U.S. - Canada Air Quality Agreement requesting Canada take undefined steps to reduce fire risk in Canada. This response from Tiffany is essentially like calling your neighbor the day their house is on fire and complaining that it’s ruining your barbeque. It’s noteworthy that these members of Congress are also finally seeing a role for the EPA they find useful - essentially serving as a complaint department for our neighbors. Whatever happened to standing up in times of crisis to help our neighbors? This version of America First actually looks more like America Alone, and most Americans know this is not who we are, and it’s not making us stronger. The fact is, after all these years, Tom Tiffany still doesn't get it. We cannot complain our way to reducing extreme climate disasters, and we cannot log our way out of the growing problem of larger, more intense wildfires. With a changing climate, we are going to see more extreme heat like we've seen this week, more severe wind events, more flash floods, and more extreme wildfires like these in the years ahead. And we need to make the investments today to reduce those risks and respond to those events. But Representative Tiffany has long been one of Washington's most dedicated zealots for disinvesting in the U.S. Forest Service and the other federal agencies that lead our responses to wildfires. And the U.S. Forest Service is right now in the midst of a reorganization that will force thousands more career managers and scientists to leave the agency and reduce our capacity to understand climate change and to respond effectively to wildfires even more. | | | | | | Climate change affects all of us, and it's not going to slow its acceleration without decisive, informed, bold action. Wisconsinites deserve representatives in Congress who understand what's at stake and who will tell the truth about what's happening to our air, water, and land – and who isn't beholden to fossil fuel company lobbyists. I want to go to Washington next year and help do that work for all of us. We'll get through this together if we work together.Please remember our state’s primary election is on August 11th. Please see details on Wisconsin voting in the section below. I hope you’ll make a plan to vote, and I would love to have your support! | | | Fred PS: On Tuesday, I was excited to announce that Congressman Mark Pocan of Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District endorsed my campaign! Mark joins former Wisconsin members of Congress David Obey, Peter Barca, Tom Barrett and Steve Kagan in supporting team Clark. The wind is in our sails and we're less then three weeks until the primary election. Be sure to make a plan to vote on August 11th! | On the Road | | | Tribal Communities Take Center Stage Powwows are some of the most important events of the year for tribal communities and an opportunity for members to come together, share traditions, food, music, and dancing, to celebrate achievements, and to recognize losses. The Lac Courte Oreilles Honor the Earth Powwow is all of that, and for hundreds of non-tribal visitors and guests, it's an education in culture and community. Seeing the Grand Entry and all of the men, women, and children dancing in their regalia accompanied by drumming circles is a powerful experience for everyone. Rick St. Germaine invited Fred to speak to the crowd after the Grand Entry where he stressed the importance of having a federal government that follows the Constitution, that respects the dignity of every person on American soil, and that honors the treaties, agreements, and solemn trust obligations we have entered into with native peoples across America. Our words should mean something and nowhere is that responsibility more important than with our commitments with our tribal nations. | | | | | Wisconsin Farm Technology Days Wisconsin's Farm Technology Days is the biggest agriculture event of the year. Farmers came from all over the state to check out the latest equipment and techniques, and folks from every walk of life showed up just to learn more about where their food comes from. This year in Stratford, it was drones and robotics next to cheese curds and lemonade — a perfect mix for a hot summer day. Our farmers feed our state and our country, and they deserve leaders who understand their challenges and show up for them.If you want to support Wisconsin agriculture, showing up to learn is one of the best places to start. And voting for representatives who will show up for farmers is one of the best ways to make sure their good work continues. | | | | | In the News | | | A New Forever War As the Iran cease fire deal negotiated by the President’s son in law and his billionaire friend Steve Witkopf has predictably fallen apart, the open hostilities in the Iran War have resumed. More American service members have been killed, and control of the Strait of Hormuz is once again being contested, and the prospects for a wider ground war can no longer be ruled out. According to , the costs of the Iran war include at least 14 American lives lost and over 400 casualties. Direct costs of military operations could be as much as $100 billion, and Americans have paid more than $68 billion in higher costs for fuel and gasoline since the war began. Longer term economic effects also include increased inflation, especially for any food or manufactured goods, and higher interest rates. These are costs that fall especially heavily on lower income Americans, especially in light of the reduction or elimination of so many federal programs that provide assistance to folks who need it. In this chaotic environment, the Administration has again ignored Congress, making it clear that today’s Congressional leadership is failing at one of their most important constitutional responsibilities. Please keep our American service members and their families in mind and pray for their safety and support. It’s time for new leadership, and the war in Iran reminds of that every day. | | | | | | Join Us for a Good Old Fashioned Phone Bank We will hold biweekly phone banking sessions on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 6-7pm. These sessions will also teach you how to conduct a phone bank if you are new to it. If you already know how to phone bank, please join us and we will get you started on making calls for Fred. Register for zoom or register for in-person at 423 E Pine Street, Washburn WI (Tuesdays only). | | | | | | | | | Do You Have a Plan to Vote? As you all probably know, we have a primary election on Tuesday, August 11th! We are confident that with your support, we will pass through the primary and use the momentum to carry us to November. But to ensure a smooth election day, we want to provide you with all the information you need to create a plan to vote. The deadline to register to vote online or by mail is July 22nd. The deadline to register at your local clerk’s office is August 7th by 5pm. And, as always, you can register to vote at your polling location on election day. To check if you are registered, you can go to myvote.wi.gov. By entering your name and birthday, you can find your registration status and polling location and request an absentee ballot.August 6th is the deadline for requesting an absentee ballot for most individuals. A completed ballot can be mailed any time before election day, and it is recommended to afford seven days before election day for your ballot to arrive. Your best bet is to drop it off in-person if you are able. In-person absentee (early) voting runs from July 28th through August 9th. You can drop your ballot off or fill one out at your municipal clerk’s office, or at another designated in your town. Check myvote.wi.gov for precise locations for early voting.For the full list of deadlines, check myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Voter-Deadlines. Voting is best done early and with a plan in mind. By voting, you are participating in your democracy and exercising a right so rare in the history of humanity.
